questions.text: What does the term ‘Hansard’ relate to?
questions.explanation: Proceedings in Parliament are broadcast on television and published in official reports called Hansard.

options.text: Official reports where proceedings in Parliament are published
A festival which celebrates the founding of the Sikh community

questions.text: Who was the first king of the House of Tudor?
questions.explanation: Henry VII (Henry Tudor)was the first king of the House of Tudor.

questions.text: What do Lewis Hamilton, Jenson Button and Damon Hill have in common?
questions.explanation: Lewis Hamilton, Jenson Button and Damon Hill have won the Formula 1 World Championship.

options.text: They have won the Formula 1 World Championship
They have won the Six Nations Championship

questions.text: According to the 2011 Census, what percentage of people said that they had no religion?
questions.explanation: According to the 2011 census,25% of peoplesaid they had no religion.

questions.text: During which period were the first coins produced in Britain?
questions.explanation: The people ofthe Iron Agehad a sophisticated culture and economy. They made the first coins to be minted in Britain, some inscribed with the names of Iron Age kings.

questions.text: What other name is given to Diwali, the religious celebration that celebrates the victory of good over evil and the gaining of knowledge?
questions.explanation: Diwali normally falls in October or November and lasts for five days. It is often calledthe Festival of Lights.

questions.text: In Wales, the jury has to listen to the evidence presented at the trial and then decide a verdict of ‘guilty’, ‘not guilty’ or ‘not proven’ based of what they have heard:
questions.explanation: The jury has to listen to the evidence presented at the trial and then decide a verdict of ‘guilty’ or ‘not guilty’ based of what they have heard. In Scotland, a third verdict of ‘not proven’ is also possible.

questions.text: The Prime Minister has a country house outside London called:
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister has a country house outside London calledChequers.

questions.text: In which English county is Maiden Castle located?
questions.explanation: A very impressive hill fort can be seen today at Maiden Castle, in the English county ofDorset.

questions.text: A National Insurance number does on its own prove to an employer that you have the right to work in the UK:
questions.explanation: A National Insurance number does not on its own prove to an employer that you have the right to work in the UK.

questions.text: Which of the following is a ceremonial role to be undertaken by the King?
questions.explanation: The King has important ceremonial roles, such asthe opening of the new parliamentary session each year. On this occasion the King makes a speech which summarises the government’s policies for the year ahead.

options.text: Opening the new parliamentary session every year
Visiting the major cities in the UK once every six months
Giving a speech on New Year’s Eve

questions.text: How long can you use your driving licence in the UK if you have a licence from another country?
questions.explanation: If you have a licence from another country, you may use it in the UKfor up to 12 months.

options.text: You need a UK driving licence
For as long as it is valid

questions.explanation: The Turing machineis a theoretical mathematical device invented by Alan Turing (1912-54), a British mathematician, in the 1930s. The theory was influential in the development of computer science and the modern-day computer.

questions.text: Which Court deals with the serious criminal offences in England, Wales and Northern Ireland?
questions.explanation: In England, Wales and Northern Ireland, serious criminal offences are tried in front of a judge and a jury in aCrown Court.

questions.text: Which famous philosopher developed ideas about human nature during the 18th century and that have continued to influence philosophers over the years?
questions.explanation: During the 18th century,David Hume’s ideas about human nature continue to influence philosophers.

questions.text: If you are arrested and taken to a police station, a police officer should:
questions.explanation: If you are arrested and taken to a police station, a police officer willtell you the reason for your arrest and you will be able to seek legal advice.

Tell you the reason for your arrest and that you will be able to seek legal advice

questions.explanation: Recent British actors to have won Oscars include Colin Firth,Sir Antony Hopkins, Dame Judi Dench, Kate Winslet and Tilda Swinton.

questions.explanation: The day before Lent starts is calledShrove Tuesday, or Pancake Day.

questions.explanation: The ‘Concorde’ began carrying passengersin 1976.

questions.explanation: Loch Lomondis the largest expanse of fresh water in mainland Britain and probably the best-known part of the park.

questions.explanation: The Chartists campaigned for every man to have the vote, elections every year, for all regions to be equal in the electoral system, secret ballots, for any man to be able to stand as an MP and for MPs to be paid.
